title: Deep learning detects breast cancer lymph node metastases after neoadjuvant therapy
summary: An interpretable deep learning pipeline was developed on a 1,027-slide set of post-neoadjuvant breast cancer lymph nodes with pathologist labels. On the post-treatment test cohort it reached slide-level AUROC 0.986 and 70.9% specificity at 100% sensitivity, and its patch heatmaps helped pathologists find and correct erroneous predictions. Independence of test and training sources was not confirmed.
ai_technology: Interpretable deep learning pipeline for slide-level classification and patch-level metastasis heatmaps
organization: Department of Medical Biophysics, University of Toronto

evidence.tested: Held-out post-neoadjuvant test cohort with pathologist labels and an interpretability study with pathologists.
evidence.unknown: Independence from training source and patient-level split not confirmed; retrospective; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning classifier and heatmap generator for lymph node slides.
